skill.name: typescript-write
skill.description: Write TypeScript and JavaScript code following Metabase coding standards and best practices. Use when developing or refactoring TypeScript/JavaScript code.
skill.summary: Guide Metabase TypeScript and JavaScript changes with tests, linting, formatting, and type checks.
skill.author: metabase

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code spans for documented yarn commands. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, dynamic command construction, or other semantic security issue in SKILL.md.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 is a Markdown inline code example for a hardcoded yarn lint command. It is not Ruby backtick execution or runtime command construction.
Line 19 documents a hardcoded yarn prettier command inside Markdown. The skill file does not execute the command or interpolate untrusted input.
Line 21 is documentation for a hardcoded yarn type-check command. The backticks are Markdown formatting, not a shell execution operator.
Line 28 shows a Markdown example for running a targeted test file. It is not executable code in the skill, and no command is dynamically built by the skill.
Line 29 documents a yarn test command with a placeholder pattern. Although a user would choose the pattern manually, the skill does not perform shell interpolation or automatic execution.
Line 34 is Markdown documentation for a hardcoded ClojureScript test command. It does not contain Ruby backtick execution or hidden command logic.

content.value_statement: Metabase code changes need consistent TypeScript, JavaScript, tests, and formatting. This skill guides development with project conventions and standard yarn checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides TypeScript and JavaScript development using Metabase coding standards.
Recommends adding failing tests before implementing fixes.
Lists linting, formatting, and type checking commands for yarn workflows.
Provides targeted JavaScript, TypeScript, and ClojureScript test commands.
Encourages small, autonomous increments within the project folder.
limitations: Does not include reusable scripts or helper files.
Does not define detailed language patterns beyond workflow guidance.
Requires the Metabase project and yarn scripts to exist.
Does not publish or commit changes automatically.

use_cases.title: Build Metabase UI Changes
use_cases.description: Develop or refactor TypeScript and JavaScript code while following local lint, format, type, and test checks.

use_cases.title: Fix Bugs With Tests
use_cases.description: Add a focused failing test, implement the fix, and verify the change with targeted project commands.

use_cases.title: Maintain Code Quality
use_cases.description: Run standard Metabase checks before handoff so reviewers see clear validation and remaining risk.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a contained TypeScript update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill. Review the relevant Metabase files, add a focused failing test, implement the smallest fix, then run targeted checks.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor JavaScript Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for cleanup without behavior changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to refactor this JavaScript area. Preserve behavior, follow nearby patterns, run formatting, and report remaining risk.

prompt_templates.title: Add Regression Coverage
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a bug fix with tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill to reproduce this bug with a failing test. Fix the issue, run the targeted test, and summarize validation.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a Cross-File Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request touching multiple TypeScript or JavaScript files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the typescript-write skill for this cross-file change. Map existing patterns, update tests first, implement in small increments, and run lint, type checks, and targeted tests.

output_examples.input: Fix a TypeScript behavior bug in a Metabase component.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation summary with tests added, files changed, validation commands run, and any review notes.

output_examples.input: Refactor a JavaScript utility without changing behavior.
output_examples.output: A focused refactor plan, completed cleanup summary, formatting status, and targeted test results.

output_examples.input: Prepare a ClojureScript-related frontend change for review.
output_examples.output: A change summary that includes relevant JavaScript or ClojureScript tests, lint status, and remaining limitations.

best_practices: Keep changes within the project folder and respect repository boundaries.
Add focused failing tests before implementation when behavior changes.
Run targeted tests plus linting, formatting, and type checks before handoff.
anti_patterns: Making broad refactors without reading nearby Metabase patterns.
Skipping tests for user-visible TypeScript or JavaScript behavior changes.
Committing changes automatically instead of leaving review to the user.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is designed for TypeScript and JavaScript work inside the Metabase repository.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents recommended yarn commands for linting, formatting, type checks, and tests.

faq.question: Can it help with ClojureScript tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It identifies the standard yarn command for running ClojureScript tests.

faq.question: Does it replace project documentation?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and should be used with current repository instructions.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large refactors?
faq.answer: Yes, but changes should be split into small, testable increments with clear validation.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
